evidence: Read the earlier separate review report and SIGN-IN.md. The earlier review covered the complete Next.js 16.4.2 to 16.4.6 upgrade diff, sign-in module and routes, migrations, roles, shared configuration and mail, dependencies, module-resolution settings, boundary and review scripts, Docker runners and hosted workflows. Application sign-in code and database boundaries are unchanged; no supported findings remain.

The earlier review read the four primary Next.js release notes, 16.4.3 through 16.4.6, including route-handler compression and the published security fixes. The current digest matches the digest calculated in that review.

The earlier reviewer ran npm ci and the disposable database chain. Bootstrap and both migration runs passed, applying four migrations on the first run. npm run handover:check passed; npm run test:handover passed 136 tests; npm test passed 313 tests across 11 files; npm run test:files passed 44 tests in one file.

The earlier reviewer ran npm run typecheck, npm run lint and npm run build; all passed, including the production build and worker bundling. npm run test:policy-fault passed with one baseline test and 139 skipped, detected the planted fault and restored the policy. npm run test:privilege-fault passed with 26 tests across two files in both baseline and restored states and detected all 22 planted faults.

The coordinator ran the hosted command npm run test:image without arguments outside the reviewer sandbox, from the template at the upgrade and rehearsal commits. It exited 0 and passed all four scenario groups: migration and repeat migration; absent, running and stopped worker heartbeats; database failure; and web and worker JSON events without credentials. The coordinator reported no labelled resources remained. This resolves the image result that withheld the earlier verdict.
Ran node scripts/sign-in-review.mjs --digest again before recording this verdict. The digest is ae4ccd2dc976b837564d3c296119578cff7e5beb1e3211eb042cce65cffba97f.
limits: No real company directory registration, external SMTP delivery, production storage permissions or complete production browser sign-in were exercised. In-process sign-in tests do not establish complete production HTTP behaviour.

The successful image result is coordinator-supplied evidence from outside the reviewer sandbox. Earlier Buildx, keychain and bootstrap failures occurred inside that sandbox. The reviewer did not rerun Docker for this verdict.

Host checks used the available local Node.js rather than the hosted operating system. The image uses its pinned Node.js 22.23.2 base. The earlier browser attempt failed at Chromium launch because macOS denied Mach port registration; the independent Python mutation baseline exited -11. The earlier review recorded both failures as local limits.
The earlier npm ci reported 25 dependency audit findings, nine moderate and sixteen high. No audit repair was attempted.
Response padding is not a constant-time guarantee under load. Deferred email delivery is not a durable queue. Multiple replicas need shared rate limiting or an ingress limit.
The digest verifies content correspondence, not reviewer identity or independence. Pull request review remains necessary.
